narrative.h2: Photoreal video is about restraint, not detail

sections.heading: What realistic actually means
sections.body: Realistic music video means the viewer doesn't think about whether it's real - which is harder than it sounds. The tells of generated video that fail at realism: too-clean skin (no pores, no asymmetry), eyes that don't have correct catchlights, hands with subtle finger-count drift, fabric that doesn't fold under gravity, motion that's too smooth (real human movement has micro-jitter). Documentary-feel realism specifically means natural light, available-source audio cues in the visual, and unposed body language.

sections.heading: Where the look comes from
sections.body: References that DPs and music-video directors actually cite: Emmanuel Lubezki's natural-light work, the Dogme 95 movement's hand-held discipline, Andrea Arnold's American Honey, Sean Baker's The Florida Project for available-light realism. Music-video specific: Hiro Murai's Childish Gambino work, anything Spike Jonze shot for Beastie Boys. Documentary photography: Alec Soth, Stephen Shore. Tunee's realistic model is trained on natural-light frames with imperfect, lived-in subjects - not glossy commercial polish.

sections.heading: Prompting tip for Tunee
sections.body: Add imperfection explicitly: 'natural skin texture with pores, slight asymmetry, available light only, no fill'. Specify time-of-day and weather: 'overcast afternoon, soft window light, no direct sun'. Hand-held motion: 'shoulder-mounted camera, subtle handheld sway'. Avoid 'photorealistic' as a bare prompt - it pushes toward CGI realism. Use 'documentary-style natural realism' instead. Real reads as imperfect; smoothness reads as rendered.
